claims.text: The initial material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has demonstrated high-temperature mechanical strength.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxidation resistance.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 2 at% Al to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al-modified alloy can be produced by standard arc melting or induction melting followed by homogenization.
Approximately 2 at% Al will selectively oxidize at the alloy surface.
Selective oxidation of Al will produce a stable, external, adherent, and effectively impermeable Al2O3-rich scale.
The Al2O3-rich scale will impede inward oxygen diffusion.
Impeded oxygen diffusion will prevent accelerated oxidation or pesting.
Relative to undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-containing alloy will show lower oxidation mass gain.
Relative to undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-containing alloy will develop a thinner oxide scale.
Relative to undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-containing alloy will retain more room-temperature tensile ductility after oxidation exposure.
Relative to undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-containing alloy will retain more high-temperature yield strength after oxidation exposure.
The proposed protection applies in air at 800–1000 °C for exposures of approximately 5–24 hours.
The protective effect is expected to persist up to approximately 1000 °C for exposures lasting hours.
Severe mechanical or thermal transients, or longer exposures at higher temperatures, may degrade the protective efficacy of the alumina scale.
The unmodified equiatomic alloy undergoes significant oxidation and associated mechanical-property degradation under similar conditions.
Excessive Al addition may reduce alloy ductility and toughness.
Failure to obtain a greater than 50% reduction in either oxide-scale thickness or mass gain, or failure to improve mechanical-property retention, would falsify the hypothesis.
